sections.title: About Crisis Text Line
sections.text: Crisis Text Line is a free, 24/7 text-based mental health support service that connects people in crisis with trained crisis counselors. Founded in 2013, Crisis Text Line has become one of the largest crisis intervention services in the United States, processing millions of text conversations with people experiencing emotional distress, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, relationship issues, and other challenges.

sections.title: Who Should Text
sections.text: Crisis Text Line is for anyone struggling with any type of crisis, not just suicide. Common reasons people text include anxiety, depression, stress, self-harm, bullying, relationship problems, eating disorders, grief, loneliness, and substance use. The service is especially popular among young people who may prefer texting over calling. You don't need to be in immediate danger to reach out—the service supports anyone who needs help.

sections.title: How to Reach Crisis Text Line
sections.text: Text HOME to 741741 from anywhere in the United States. You can also text from Canada (text HOME to 686868), UK (text HELLO to 85258), or Ireland (text HELLO to 50808). The service is completely free—standard text messaging rates may apply depending on your phone plan. Conversations are confidential and secure.

sections.title: What to Expect When You Text
sections.text: When you text HOME to 741741, you'll receive an automated response while being connected to a live, trained crisis counselor. The counselor will introduce themselves and ask how they can help. They'll listen, provide emotional support, and help you work through your feelings using evidence-based techniques. Conversations typically last 15-45 minutes but can go longer if needed. You can end the conversation at any time.

sections.title: About Crisis Counselors
sections.text: Crisis Text Line counselors are trained volunteers who complete a rigorous 30-hour training program and ongoing education. They are supervised by licensed clinical professionals during every shift. Counselors use collaborative problem-solving and active listening techniques to help texters move from a hot moment to a cool calm. The service uses data and technology to improve crisis intervention while maintaining strict privacy standards.

sections.title: Privacy and Safety
sections.text: Crisis Text Line takes privacy seriously. Conversations are encrypted and confidential. The organization maintains strict data protection policies and does not share personal information with third parties without consent. In rare cases where there is immediate danger to life, Crisis Text Line may contact emergency services—but this happens in less than 1% of conversations. The service is designed to be discreet, making it easier for people in sensitive situations to reach out for help without others knowing.

sections.title: Beyond the Text Line
sections.text: After your conversation, Crisis Text Line can connect you with local resources, ongoing mental health services, and additional support. The organization's website offers self-help resources, information about mental health conditions, and guidance for supporting loved ones in crisis. Crisis Text Line also partners with schools, workplaces, and organizations to bring crisis support to more communities. The service has answered millions of text conversations and continues to expand its reach to help more people in need.
